paragraph_content.content: EUROPE METALS & MINING

title_content.content: Lifting Copper Prices on Ex-US Tightness Ahead of US Tariff Catalyst. Buy LUN, ANTO.

paragraph_content.content: The GS commodities team sees a materially tighter ex-US copper market through 2026-27, driven by both weaker mine supply and continued tariff related shifts in trade flow. Global mine supply has been is reduced by ~350kt (~1.5% global mine supply) in 2026 and 2027, primarily reflecting slower recoveries at Grasberg and Kamoa-Kakula (full recovery expected in 2028), while scrap is not offsetting refined tightness, given weaker China domestic availability. At the same time, stronger US imports in H1'26 continue to pull metal out of the ex-US system, with US inventories expected to build by ~900kt in 2026 (vs 550kt previously) to ~1.8Mt by year end (from ~0.1Mt at beginning of 2025). The team believe this will drive a material step change in the ex-US balance to deficits of ~640kt/170kt in 2026/27, tightening the global market where the LME price is set, underpinning higher pricing.

The key near term catalyst in our view is the tariff outcome (expected this month) for the US. A Jan'27 tariff introduction would likely pull forward more US imports, further tightening the ex-US market and potentially pushing LME prices above US$14k/t in 2H'26, before easing in 2027 as flows normalise, which would present further upside risk to our base case forecast. If no news is announced on tariffs, prices could remain supported around current levels, given ex-US tightness and positioning. Conversely, a definitive “no tariff” outcome would reduce the ex-US deficit and could flip 2027 back into surplus, weighing on prices towards ~$12.8k/t, where the team see the fundamental/fair value for copper.

We reflect our commodities team's latest published copper prices into our models for copper exposed names (ANTO, LUN, GLEN, AAL, RIO, BHP), alongside Q2'26 quarter to date MtM updates for commodity prices. We also roll forward our valuations by 6 months to Jun'27. We make no operating changes to our forward estimates with this update. Across our copper-exposed names, we continue to prefer:

LUN (Buy) on (1) Relative Valuation: ~1x P/NAV vs peers at 1.5x-2x P/NAV (VA Consensus Data). (2) Leverage to copper: copper revenue now represents 85% of the total, one of the highest in the sector; (2) demonstrating strong operational performance, through continued production performance and cost discipline; (3) Growth catalysts ahead: Vicuna RIGI approval and FID in late 2026.

paragraph_content.content: ■ ANTO (Buy) on (1) Copper gold leverage and scarcity premium: stands out as one of the few scalable, pure European copper gold equities, positioning it to capture the copper equity premium as investors seek targeted exposure to these commodities. (2) Proven execution and credible medium term growth targets: one of the few companies delivering growth in copper currently. The portfolio is anchored by Centinela and Pelambres, which together account for ~80% of current output and will drive ~95% of production growth this decade, on our estimates. (3) Centinela expansion is the key: The second concentrator (C2) progressing as planned. Market is not fully appreciating the other brownfield growth options, including the C2E expansion. C2 + C2E could position Centinela as the largest, lowest cost, and primary growth driver this decade.

content.html:
Investment thesis
BHP1. Limited upside: BHP is currently trading at 1x NAV vs RIO at 0.8x NAV and 7.6x FY26E EBITDA (25y avg ~6-7x) vs. RIO at 6.8x FY26E EBITDA. That said, we believe this premium vs. peers can be partly maintained due to ongoing superior margins and operating performance2. Optionality with +US$40-50bn copper pipeline, but growth and FCF/t below RIO in copper3. Robust FCF, but still below RIO: BHP is trading on a FCF/DPS yield of c. 4%/3% over the next 12-m, below RIO on 6%/4%. We now see BHP's minerals capex increasing to ~US$10-11bn by mid-decade (above peer RIO at ~US$9-10bn).
RIO1. Limited Upside: Trading at c. 0.8x NAV (GBP95/sh), c.7x FY26E EBITDA vs peer average of 1x NAV and 6.5x FY26E EBITDA2. FCF and dividend yield: FCF/dividend yield in 2026 (c. 5%/4% yield) & 2027 (c. 6%/4% yield)3. Production growth through 2030: Rio is a FCF story in our view, with forecast CuEq production growth of ~10% through 2030 driven by the ramp-up of the Oyu Tolgoi UG copper mine & a recovery at Escondida and Bingham4. Pilbara turnaround (~50% group NAV): the potential for FCF/t improvement in the Pilbara with Gudai-Darri and over the medium to long run driven by Rhodes Ridge, with a medium term capacity target of 345-360Mt
GLEN1. Valuation: The stock is trading at c. 1.07x NAV (GBP5.7/sh) and 5.3x FY26E EBITDA2. FCF conversion: FCF yield of c. 7% in FY26E and 7% in FY27E (c. 9% at spot), driven mostly by cash harvesting (low capex) from energy assets, but commodity prices remain subdued3. Lower capital-intensive copper growth optionality: we model an increase of ~30% in copper production from 2025 to 2029, to ~1Mtpa, at a cost of US$18-20k/t, consistent with the brownfield nature of its growth options, and lower than other recently announced major projects in the industry
ANTO1. High margin core business which generates c.90% of EBITDA, centred on low cost copper mines2. Assets host large resources that can underpin multi-decade operations, and new breakthrough leaching technologies could help squeeze additional low-cost tonnes3. The second concentrator (C2) progressing as planned. Market is not fully appreciating the other brownfield growth options, including the C2E expansion. C2 + C2E could position Centinela as the largest, lowest cost, and primary growth driver this decade.
LUN1. Following sales of Neves-Corvo and Zinkgruvan, copper now accounts for 85-90% of revenue (compared to ~70% previously), hence we apply a multiple of 10x since LUN is now a pure play copper player2. Developing Vicuna offers exposure to a large scale, multi generational copper project with future expansion potential. Their JV partner in Vicuña, BHP, contributes best-in-class project development, financing support, and technical expertise in managing large-scale open-pit copper operations3. Existing asset base to support dividend yields, with excess capital driving the next leg of expansion over the medium term

The GS Factor Profile provides investment context for a stock by comparing key attributes to the market (i.e. our universe of rated stocks) and its sector peers. The four key attributes depicted are: Growth, Financial Returns, Multiple (e.g. valuation) and Integrated (a composite of Growth, Financial Returns and Multiple). Growth, Financial Returns and Multiple are calculated by using normalized ranks for specific metrics for each stock. The normalized ranks for the metrics are then averaged and converted into percentiles for the relevant attribute. The precise calculation of each metric may vary depending on the fiscal year, industry and region, but the standard approach is as follows:

Growth is based on a stock's forward-looking sales growth, EBITDA growth and EPS growth (for financial stocks, only EPS and sales growth), with a higher percentile indicating a higher growth company. Financial Returns is based on a stock's forward-looking ROE, ROCE and CROCI (for financial stocks, only ROE), with a higher percentile indicating a company with higher financial returns. Multiple is based on a stock's forward-looking P/E, P/B, price/dividend (P/D), EV/EBITDA, EV/FCF and EV/Debt Adjusted Cash Flow (DACF) (for financial stocks, only P/E, P/B and P/D), with a higher percentile indicating a stock trading at a higher multiple. The Integrated percentile is calculated as the average of the Growth percentile, Financial Returns percentile and (100% - Multiple percentile).

Financial Returns and Multiple use the GS analyst forecasts at the fiscal year-end at least three quarters in the future. Growth uses inputs for the fiscal year at least seven quarters in the future compared with the year at least three quarters in the future (on a per-share basis for all metrics).
For a more detailed description of how we calculate the GS Factor Profile, please contact your GS representative.

Across our global coverage, we examine stocks using an M&A framework, considering both qualitative factors and quantitative factors (which may vary across sectors and regions) to incorporate the potential that certain companies could be acquired. We then assign a M&A rank as a means of scoring companies under our rated coverage from 1 to 3, with 1 representing high (30%-50%) probability of the company becoming an acquisition target, 2 representing medium (15%-30%) probability and 3 representing low (0%-15%) probability. For companies ranked 1 or 2, in line with our standard departmental guidelines we incorporate an M&A component into our target price. M&A rank of 3 is considered immaterial and therefore does not factor into our price target, and may or may not be discussed in research.
